name.en: PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana (National Pension Scheme for Traders)

authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India

description.en: Pradhan Mantri Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana is a government-sponsored pension scheme for small traders, shopkeepers, and self-employed persons. Enrolled beneficiaries receive a minimum assured monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 after attaining the age of 60 years. The scheme operates on a voluntary and contributory basis, with matching contribution from the Central Government. It is administered through the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) as the Pension Fund Manager and Common Service Centres (CSCs) for enrolment.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All applicants — must be between 18 and 40 years of age at the time of enrolment
verifiedConditions.claim: The applicant must be between 18 and 40 years of age at the time of joining the scheme. The entry age determines the monthly contribution amount.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All applicants — annual turnover must not exceed Rs. 1.5 crore
verifiedConditions.claim: The applicant must be a small trader, shopkeeper, or self-employed person with an annual turnover not exceeding Rs. 1.5 crore (Rs. 15,000,000).

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All applicants — must not be a beneficiary of EPFO, NPS, or PM-SYM
verifiedConditions.claim: The applicant must not be covered under the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), the National Pension System (NPS), or Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan Yojana (PM-SYM).

unverifiedEligibility: Income tax payers may or may not be eligible depending on specific notification updates.
The definition of self-employed persons eligible for the scheme may be interpreted differently by enrolment centres.
Family pension provisions for the spouse after the subscriber's death may apply at 50% of the pension amount.

requirements.claim: Valid Aadhaar card of the applicant. Aadhaar number is used for identity verification and is linked to the pension account.
Active savings bank account with IFSC code. Monthly contributions are auto-debited from this account.
Active mobile number linked to Aadhaar for OTP-based verification during enrolment.
GSTIN (Goods and Services Tax Identification Number) if registered under GST, or a self-declaration of annual turnover not exceeding Rs. 1.5 crore if not GST-registered.
Proof of age as recorded in Aadhaar. The age at entry determines the monthly contribution amount ranging from Rs. 55 (age 18) to Rs. 200 (age 40).

processInformation.appliesTo: All applicants enrolling through Common Service Centre
processInformation.claim: Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with Aadhaar card and savings bank passbook or bank statement. Alternatively, the applicant may self-enrol through the Maandhan portal (maandhan.in) or the PM-SYM/PM Laghu Vyapari mobile app.

Aadhaar number is verified using OTP sent to the linked mobile number. Name, date of birth, and address are auto-populated from Aadhaar. The applicant confirms the details and provides bank account information with IFSC code.

An auto-debit mandate is set up on the subscriber's savings bank account for monthly contribution. The contribution amount is determined by the entry age: Rs. 55 per month for age 18, scaling up to Rs. 200 per month for age 40. The Central Government contributes an equal matching amount.
A Vyapari Pension Card is generated with a unique Vyapari Pension Account Number (VPAN). The subscriber receives confirmation via SMS and can track their account through the Maandhan portal.

output.claim: Upon successful enrolment, the subscriber receives a Vyapari Pension Card with a unique Vyapari Pension Account Number (VPAN). The subscriber is entitled to a minimum assured monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 after attaining the age of 60 years. The pension is deposited directly into the subscriber's bank account. In case of the subscriber's death, the spouse receives 50% of the pension as family pension.

fees.applicability: Monthly contribution for entry age 18 years (minimum). Ranges from Rs. 55 to Rs. 200 depending on age at entry.
fees.claim: The monthly contribution ranges from Rs. 55 (for entry at age 18) to Rs. 200 (for entry at age 40). The Central Government makes an equal matching contribution to the subscriber's pension fund. There is no separate registration or processing fee. The contribution is auto-debited from the subscriber's savings bank account.

fees.applicability: One-time enrolment processing at Common Service Centre
fees.claim: There is no enrolment fee charged to the subscriber. The cost of enrolment at Common Service Centres is borne by the Government of India. Self-enrolment through the Maandhan portal is also free of charge.

processingTime.applicability: Enrolment and account activation from submission of application
processingTime.claim: Enrolment is processed immediately at the Common Service Centre or through the Maandhan portal. The Vyapari Pension Account is activated on the same day upon successful Aadhaar verification and auto-debit mandate setup. The first contribution is debited in the same or next billing cycle.

sources.title: Maandhan Portal — PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana Official Enrolment System
sources.publisher: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Maandhan portal is the official enrolment and account management platform for PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana. It provides online self-enrolment, contribution tracking, and pension account management for small traders, shopkeepers, and self-employed persons with annual turnover up to Rs. 1.5 crore.
claimsSupported: Minimum assured pension of Rs. 3,000 per month after age 60.
Monthly contribution ranges from Rs. 55 to Rs. 200 based on entry age.
Equal matching contribution from the Central Government.
Aadhaar and savings bank account are mandatory for enrolment.
No enrolment fee is charged to the subscriber.
sources.uncertainty: Contribution amounts and pension benefits may be revised by the Government.

sources.title: Ministry of Labour and Employment — Social Security Schemes
sources.publisher: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Ministry of Labour and Employment administers PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana as a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for small traders and self-employed persons. LIC of India is the Pension Fund Manager. The scheme excludes persons covered under EPFO, NPS, or PM-SYM.
claimsSupported: Scheme is for small traders with turnover up to Rs. 1.5 crore.
Beneficiaries of EPFO, NPS, or PM-SYM are not eligible.
Family pension of 50% to spouse upon subscriber's death.
LIC of India is the Pension Fund Manager.
sources.uncertainty: Eligibility criteria for income tax payers may be subject to revision.

limitations: The scheme is voluntary and contributory — benefits are available only if contributions are made regularly until age 60.
If contributions are discontinued, exit provisions allow partial withdrawal with reduced benefits depending on the duration of contributions.
The pension amount of Rs. 3,000 per month is the minimum assured and may not account for inflation over the contribution period.
The scheme does not cover persons already enrolled in EPFO, NPS, or PM-SYM.
This record does not cover the detailed exit and withdrawal rules for premature closure.
The definition of eligible self-employed persons and the turnover limit may be revised by the Government.
